verses.1: Let my soul bless the LORD, and let all that is within me bless his holy name.
verses.2: Let my soul bless the LORD, and never forget all his blessings.
verses.3: The one who forgives all your sins, who heals all your diseases,
verses.4: the one who redeems your life from the grave, who crowns you with steadfast love and mercy,
verses.5: who satisfies you with good things, so that your youth renews itself like the eagle.
verses.6: The LORD does righteous acts and executes justice for all the oppressed.
verses.7: He made known his ways to Moses, his acts to the people of Israel.
verses.8: The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.
verses.9: He will not always be angry, nor will he keep his wrath forever.
verses.10: He does not treat us as our sins deserve, nor repay us according to our iniquities.
verses.11: For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his steadfast love toward those who fear him.
verses.12: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.
verses.13: Like a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him.
verses.14: For he knows our frame; he remembers that we are dust.
verses.15: Human beings are like grass; their days are like the flowers of the field.
verses.16: The wind passes over them and they are gone, and their place no longer knows them.
verses.17: But the steadfast love of the LORD is from forever to forever, and his righteousness to all generations.
verses.18: To all who keep his covenant and remember to do his commandments,
verses.19: the LORD has established his throne in the heavens, and his sovereignty rules over all.
verses.20: Bless the LORD, you his angels, you mighty in strength who do his word, who listen to the voice of his word.
verses.21: Bless the LORD, all his hosts, his ministers who do his will.
verses.22: Bless the LORD, all his works, in all places of his dominion. Let my soul bless the LORD.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "all that is within me" reflects the Hebrew "כָּל־קְרָבַי" which literally means "all that is near to me" but is rendered here as a poetic expression of total being.
- v. 12: "transgressions" is used for "פְּשָׁעֵינוּ" (our rebellions/iniquities), consistent with the glossary's treatment of sin terms.
- v. 17: "from forever to forever" is a natural English rendering of "מֵעוֹלָם וְעַד־עוֹלָם" to capture the timeless extent of God’s steadfast love.
- v. 19: "his sovereignty rules over all" reflects the phrase "מָשָׁלָה" (rules) used with a broad, cosmic sense.
